pages.text: UK Reader Awards 2026: Winners Revealed | National Geographic By Editors of National Geographic Traveller (UK) Published September 30, 2026 This article was produced by National Geographic Traveller (UK). It’s been an interesting year in travel — more reason than ever for us to reinstate our Reader Awards. We wanted to know what inspires you when booking a trip and where’s really captured your imagination in the past year. What came across most keenly was your continuing desire to explore, seek out new experiences and connect with both the environment and other cultures. The winners’ list indicates a return to familiar destinations on the UK’s doorstep, perhaps a reflection of the challenges — tight finances, fractious politics, Middle East strife — that have affected travel in 2026. But more far-flung destinations are also among the 16 category finalists, testament to your unshakeable enthusiasm for adventure. People’s Choice: Italy Food and beauty are the secular religions that elevate Italy to another level. No brochure flags up either directly. Why would they? Both are factored into the equation wherever you go, whether to Naples for pizza, Florence for art or Sardinia for improbably perfect beaches. Runner-up Japan equally justifies its popularity. Now almost a bargain due to persistent low inflation and a weak yen, the country remains distinct in an increasingly homogenised world. GEOIDs are numeric codes that uniquely identify all administrative/legal and statistical geographic areas for which the Census Bureau tabulates data. pages.text: Understanding the Gospel of Nat Turner Skip to main content Fox Searchlight On August 27, 1831, the Richmond Compiler asked: “Who is this Nat Turner?” At the time, Turner was hiding in Southampton, Virginia, not far from the site where he launched the most important slave revolt in American history. Nat Turner’s Revolt, which had taken place just five days earlier, had left more than 50 whites dead; by the time the trials finished, a similar number of suspected rebels were either killed extra legally or condemned and executed. Even when Nat Turner was captured, on October 30, 1831, the Compiler’s question had remained unanswered. As a result, a white lawyer, Thomas R. Gray, arranged to go to the jail where Turner was held awaiting his trial and take down what Turner described as “a history of the motives which induced me to undertake the late insurrection.” Over the last decade, scholars working with other sources and doing close textual analysis of The Confessions of Nat Turner have become increasingly confident that Gray transcribed Turner’s confession, with, as Gray claimed, “little or no variation.” While The Confessions of Nat Turner remains the ur-text for anyone who wants to understand Nat Turner, this 5,000-word account creates as many questions as it answers. As a result, the document has become a springboard for artists who want to imagine the life of the most famous American to rebel against slavery. OLMS also administers the standards of conduct provisions of the Civil Service Reform Act of 1978 ( CSRA ) and the Foreign Service Act of 1980, which extend comparable protections to Federal labor unions. A union that represents only employees of state, county, or municipal governments is not subject to the LMRDA or the CSRA. Accuracy also varies widely across 13 different languages, reflecting differences in available training data, with better outcomes in English, French, Spanish and Portuguese and lower marks in languages such as Hindi, Urdu and Swahili. pages.text: Universal Design | U.S. Department of Labor Skip to main content Universal Design More in This Section Close Accessible Technology Communications Access Health Care Housing Personal Assistance Services Transportation Universal Design Universal design (UD) is a strategy for making products, environments, operational systems, and services welcoming and usable to the widest range of people possible. The key principles of UD are simplicity, flexibility, and efficiency. Whether we realize it or not, most of us benefit from UD on a daily basis. Originally developed in response to the needs of the aging population and people with disabilities, UD now increases access to products, places, and services for all populations. Companies that embrace UD in their facilities, programs, and services recognize that their workforce and customers have a broad range of abilities, ages, reading levels, learning styles, languages, etc.—and an even wider variety of needs and expectations. Good customer service means providing every customer with a welcoming environment, respectful treatment, and needed information. This goes for the workforce as well. UD provides an important tool set for companies seeking to provide such advantages for both their customers and their employees. UD is a lens through which every aspect of a business can be viewed, and a set of tools by which products, services, customer satisfaction, and employee attraction and retention can be improved. At its height, it was the largest city in the Americas, spanning nearly eight miles. It boasted complex irrigation canals for farming and teemed with skilled artisans who crafted unparalleled gold and silver metalwork. The city thrived from around A.D. 900 to 1470—when it was conquered by the burgeoning Inca Empire. Now, researchers excavating the city’s ruins have reported a once-in-a-lifetime discovery of unlooted tombs, revealing a new window into the elusive and little-known Chimú elites. The discovery, announced last week by Peru’s Ministry of Culture, will help contextualize previous Chimú findings and reshape archaeologists’ understanding of their enigmatic culture. “Prior to this discovery, what was known about elite Chimú tombs came from platforms that had been looted and destroyed since colonial times,” Jorges Meneses, the archaeologist in charge of the excavation, said in a statement from the Ministry of Culture. From the 38 skeletons and various artifacts he and his colleagues recovered at the site, the archaeologists will now—for the first time—be able to piece together fragmentary evidence of the Chimú elite to better understand how they lived and governed one of Peru’s most formidable empires. Urinary Tract Infection Basics For Everyone Sept. 22, 2026 Español Key points Do you have pain or burning when you urinate? You might have a urinary tract infection (UTI). UTIs are common infections that happen when bacteria enter the urethra and infect the urinary tract. Antibiotics treat UTIs. A healthcare professional can determine if you have a UTI and what antibiotic you need. Overview The urinary tract includes the bladder, urethra and kidneys (see figure). Urinary tract infections or UTIs are common infections that happen when bacteria, often from the skin or rectum, enter the urethra and infect the urinary tract. Female urinary tract Bacteria from the skin or rectum can travel up the urethra and cause a bladder infection. Types A bladder infection (cystitis) is the most common type of UTI. A k idney infection (pyelonephritis) is less common than bladder infection but is more serious. pages.description: Nvidia has been caught in a tug-of-war between the US and China as the countries compete for AI dominance.
pages.text: US approves sale of Nvidia's advanced H200 chips to China Skip to content Site search Home News Sport Business Technology Health Culture Arts Travel Earth Audio Video Live Documentaries Weather Newsletters Watch Live US approves sale of Nvidia's advanced AI chips to China 14 January 2026 Share Save Add as preferred on Google Osmond Chia Business reporter Getty Images Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang The US government has given chip giant Nvidia the green light to sell its advanced artificial intelligence (AI) processors in China, the Department of Commerce said on Tuesday. The H200, Nvidia's second-most-advanced semiconductor, had been restricted by Washington over concerns that it would give China's technology industry and military an edge over the US. The Commerce Department said the chips can be shipped to China granted that there is sufficient supply of the processors in the US. President Donald Trump said last month that he would allow the chip sales to "approved customers" in China and collect a 25% fee. Nvidia's spokesperson told the BBC that the company welcomed the move, saying it will benefit manufacturing and jobs in the US. The Commerce Department's Bureau of Industry and Security said its revised export policy applies to Nvidia's H200 chips, as well as less advanced processors. Chinese customers must also show "sufficient security procedures" and cannot use the chips for military uses. The shooting began on Thursday morning local time inside a gym in an apartment building in the Logan Circle neighbourhood, which is about a mile (1.6km) north of the White House. Police said the suspect, identified as 55-year-old doctor Matt Wade Lambert, then barricaded himself in an apartment, and later died of a self-inflicted gunshot wound. While the suspect was barricaded, "he did fire through the door at officers at least on two occasions", Jefferey Carroll, the interim chief of the Metropolitan Police Department, said at a news conference.
